primitives.note: Spirit Abjuration: damaging basic attacks/abilities apply a stack (cap 3, 4s duration, refreshes) to the target; the 3rd stack consumes all stacks for bonus damage.
P's proc damage scales off target's max health; Q's recast bolt damage scales linearly from base (0% missing health) to 1.5x base (100% missing health).
Twofold Hex outbound bolt marks the target, then a manual or automatic recast fires a return bolt that expunges the mark for separate damage.
The Weirding and the shockwave portion of Between Worlds deal a single fixed-formula magic damage instance on cast.
Mana costs (60/80/100) against a limited mana pool can cap how many Q/E/R cycles fit in the 15s window.

P's per-second heal from active Spirits, and W/R's invisibility, ghosting, bonus movement speed, displacement immunity and untargetability are pure survival/mobility effects irrelevant to the damage fight and (per the mobility-is-ignored rule) largely irrelevant to the survival fight too, except P's heal which changes effective health taken.

needsBespoke.why: Every damage-relevant mechanic (stack-and-consume passive, missing-health-scaled recast, plain-cast E/R, mana budget) is expressible with existing primitives once the single-dummy simplification is applied (only one Abjuration cycle and one active Q mark can exist on a single target at a time, so the kit's multi-target-only wrinkles, like Q's reduced subsequent-bolt damage, never trigger).

proposal: Open the fight by casting R (Between Worlds) on the dummy for its shockwave magic damage and Realm Hopper buff, since its cooldown (100-140s) is far longer than the 15s window and it should only ever be cast once.
Immediately follow with Q (Twofold Hex) outbound cast to hit the dummy, dealing damage, applying a mark, and adding a Spirit Abjuration stack.
Weave in a basic attack (also applies a Spirit Abjuration stack) while waiting out Q's 0.1s recast-enable delay.
Cast E (The Weirding) for its flat magic damage and a further Spirit Abjuration stack.

Manually recast Q as soon as the 0.1s window opens (rather than letting it auto-recast at the mark's 3.5s expiry) to maximize ability uptime and DPS, dealing the return-bolt damage scaled by the dummy's current missing health.

Repeat the Q cast-recast cycle on cooldown (~7-9s full cycle depending on rank) for the rest of the 15s, weaving E on its own cooldown (~11-15s) and basic attacks in between to keep stacking/consuming Spirit Abjuration for its bonus max-health-based damage roughly every third damaging hit.
Do not cast W (Across the Veil) at any point: it deals no damage and only grants invisibility, ghosting and bonus movement speed, none of which matter against a stationary, non-attacking dummy.
questions: Should Q's recast be fired immediately after the 0.1s delay for uptime, or deliberately delayed toward the mark's 3.5s expiry so the missing-health scaling benefits from a lower dummy health percentage, and does the delay cost more DPS than it gains?

Does the simulator model Aurora's basic attacks between ability casts (needed to help build Spirit Abjuration stacks and use Runaan's-style on-hit interactions), or is the rotation ability-casts-only?

At what point (level/items) does Aurora's mana pool actually become the binding constraint on repeating the Q/E cycle for the full 15 seconds, given Q+E costs 140 mana per full cycle plus R's 100 mana up front?

Is R best opened at the very start of the fight for maximum total damage window, or held briefly so its long cast-to-cooldown-start delay (post-effect) doesn't waste time that could instead go to Q/E cycles?
